material_id:
Hari ketujuh: kita belajar membaca **seragam** kata, yaitu akhirannya. Dari akhiran, kita tahu sebuah kata bekerja sebagai benda, sifat, keterangan, atau kerja. Di Listening kita mencatat angka dan urutan dalam kuliah, dan di Reading kita menaklukkan soal NOT/EXCEPT.

=== listening
## Mencatat lecture: topik, angka, urutan
Dosen sering memberi **penanda urutan**: *First, Second, And third, Finally, After that, Later*. Dosen juga menyebut **angka**: tahun, jumlah, persentase. Catat dengan singkat: angka + kata kerja (*1840 jual*, *2x lipat*). Soal Part C hampir selalu menanyakan salah satunya.
Perumpamaan: mencatat lecture itu seperti menulis daftar belanja saat mendengar resep di radio. Kamu tidak menyalin semua kalimat, cukup bahan, jumlah, dan urutannya.
> First/Second/Finally → nomori catatan · tahun/jumlah → tulis angka + kata kerja
✓ Dengar topik di kalimat pembuka (*Today we're going to talk about…*)
✓ Pasangkan setiap angka dengan kejadiannya
✓ Soal NOT di lecture: centang yang disebut, sisakan yang tidak
✕ Menukar dua angka yang mirip (1843 vs 1847)
✕ Memilih jawaban karena kata yang sama tetapi kejadiannya berbeda

=== structure
## Word form: akhiran menentukan kelas kata
[[suffix]] (akhiran) adalah seragam kata. Akhiran **noun**: *-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance/-ence, -ery*. Akhiran **adjective**: *-ous, -ive, -ful, -al, -ic, -ent/-ant*. Akhiran **adverb**: biasanya *-ly*. Akhiran **verb**: *-ize, -en, -ify*. Lihat posisinya: setelah *the/a/his* butuh noun; sebelum noun butuh adjective; menerangkan verb butuh adverb.
Perumpamaan: akhiran itu seperti seragam kerja. Dari seragamnya kamu tahu dia satpam, perawat, atau koki. Kalau seragamnya salah, ia salah tempat.
> the/a/his + ___ → noun · ___ + noun → adjective · verb + ___ → adverb
✓ an important **discovery** · a **significant** effect · spoke **enthusiastically**
✓ The **construction** took two years.
✓ physical and mental **health**
✕ a **clearly** explanation (sebelum noun butuh adjective)
✕ The **govern** announced… (setelah *The* butuh noun)

=== reading
## Soal NOT / EXCEPT
Soal *All of the following … EXCEPT* atau *Which is NOT mentioned* meminta satu pilihan yang **tidak** sesuai teks. Strategi: temukan bagian teks yang dimaksud, lalu **centang** setiap pilihan yang memang tertulis. Pilihan yang tersisa adalah jawabannya. Waspadai pilihan yang memakai kata dari teks tetapi membalik maknanya.
Perumpamaan: soal EXCEPT itu seperti absen kelas. Panggil satu per satu; yang tidak menjawab **hadir** itulah jawabannya.
> Cari bagian teks → centang 3 pilihan yang ada → sisakan 1
✓ Baca soal dua kali: apakah yang dicari yang BENAR atau yang TIDAK?
✓ Cek angka dan waktu dengan teliti (sebelum 1500 vs awal abad 17)
✕ Memilih pilihan pertama yang terlihat benar (lupa kata NOT)
✕ Mencentang pilihan hanya karena ada satu kata yang sama
material_en:
Day seven: we learn to read a word's **uniform**, its ending. The ending tells you whether a word works as a noun, adjective, adverb, or verb. In Listening we note numbers and sequence in lectures, and in Reading we conquer NOT/EXCEPT questions.

=== listening
## Lecture notes: topic, numbers, sequence
Lecturers often give **sequence markers**: *First, Second, And third, Finally, After that, Later*. They also give **numbers**: years, amounts, percentages. Note them briefly: number + verb (*1840 on sale*, *2x*). Part C questions almost always ask about one of them.
Analogy: taking lecture notes is like writing a shopping list while hearing a recipe on the radio. You don't copy every sentence, just the ingredients, amounts, and order.
> First/Second/Finally → number your notes · years/amounts → write number + verb
✓ Hear the topic in the opening line (*Today we're going to talk about…*)
✓ Pair each number with its event
✓ NOT questions in lectures: tick what was said, keep what wasn't
✕ Swapping two similar numbers (1843 vs 1847)
✕ Choosing an answer for a shared word when the event is different

=== structure
## Word form: the ending decides the job
A [[suffix]] is a word's uniform. **Noun** endings: *-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance/-ence, -ery*. **Adjective** endings: *-ous, -ive, -ful, -al, -ic, -ent/-ant*. **Adverb** endings: usually *-ly*. **Verb** endings: *-ize, -en, -ify*. Then check the slot: after *the/a/his* you need a noun; before a noun, an adjective; describing a verb, an adverb.
Analogy: an ending is a work uniform. From the uniform you know who's the guard, the nurse, or the cook. In the wrong uniform, they're in the wrong place.
> the/a/his + ___ → noun · ___ + noun → adjective · verb + ___ → adverb
✓ an important **discovery** · a **significant** effect · spoke **enthusiastically**
✓ The **construction** took two years.
✓ physical and mental **health**
✕ a **clearly** explanation (before a noun you need an adjective)
✕ The **govern** announced… (after *The* you need a noun)

=== reading
## NOT / EXCEPT questions
*All of the following … EXCEPT* or *Which is NOT mentioned* asks for the one option that does **not** match the text. Strategy: find the relevant part, then **tick** each option that really is written there. The one left over is the answer. Watch for options that reuse the text's words but reverse their meaning.
Analogy: an EXCEPT question is a roll call. Call each name; the one who doesn't answer **present** is your answer.
> Find the passage part → tick the 3 that appear → keep the 1 left
✓ Read the question twice: are you looking for what IS true or what is NOT?
✓ Check numbers and dates carefully (before 1500 vs the early 1600s)
✕ Picking the first option that looks true (forgetting the NOT)
✕ Ticking an option just because one word matches

script.speaker: W1
script.text: How many pages does the history report need to be?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: At least ten, but Professor Kim said no more than fifteen.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about the report?
options: It must be exactly ten pages.
It should be between ten and fifteen pages.
It is due in fifteen days.
It can be as long as the students want.
questions.key_sentence: At least ten, but Professor Kim said no more than fifteen.
questions.key_translation_id: Minimal sepuluh, tapi Profesor Kim bilang tidak boleh lebih dari lima belas.
questions.why_correct_id: **At least ten** artinya minimal sepuluh halaman. **no more than fifteen** artinya maksimal lima belas. Jadi panjang laporannya harus di antara sepuluh sampai lima belas halaman.
questions.why_correct_en: **At least ten** means a minimum of ten pages. **no more than fifteen** means a maximum of fifteen. So it's between ten and fifteen pages.

why_wrong_id.0: **At least ten** artinya boleh lebih dari sepuluh, bukan harus pas sepuluh.
why_wrong_id.2: **Fifteen** itu batas halaman, bukan jumlah hari sampai tenggat.
why_wrong_id.3: Ada batas atasnya kok: nggak lebih dari lima belas.

why_wrong_en.0: **At least ten** allows more than ten, not exactly ten.
why_wrong_en.2: **Fifteen** is the page limit, not days until the deadline.
why_wrong_en.3: There's an upper limit: no more than fifteen.

questions.analogy_id: **At least** dan **no more than** itu kayak pagar di dua sisi jalan. Kamu bebas jalan di mana aja di antara keduanya.
questions.analogy_en: **At least** and **no more than** are fences on both sides of a road. Walk anywhere between them.
questions.tip_id: **at least** itu minimal. **no more than** atau **at most** itu maksimal. Gabungin jadi rentang.
questions.tip_en: **at least** is the minimum. **no more than** or **at most** is the maximum. Put them together as a range.

script.speaker: W2
script.text: It closed at six, but the one in the student center stays open until nine.

questions.prompt: What does the woman imply?
options: The man can still buy books at another store.
The man should come back tomorrow at six.
The student center closed at six.
questions.key_sentence: It closed at six, but the one in the student center stays open until nine.
questions.key_translation_id: Toko itu tutup jam enam, tapi yang di gedung kemahasiswaan buka sampai jam sembilan.
questions.why_correct_id: Toko yang ditanyain udah tutup jam enam. Tapi **the one in the student center stays open until nine**, ada toko lain yang masih buka. Jadi si pria masih bisa beli buku di toko lain itu.
questions.why_correct_en: The bookstore he asked about closed at six. But **the one in the student center stays open until nine**. So he can still buy books there.

why_wrong_id.1: Dia nggak nyuruh datang besok. Dia nunjukin toko lain yang masih buka.
why_wrong_id.2: Yang tutup jam enam itu toko pertama. Toko di gedung kemahasiswaan buka sampai jam sembilan.
why_wrong_id.3: Kebalikannya. Satu toko masih buka.

why_wrong_en.1: She doesn't say come back tomorrow. She points to another open store.
why_wrong_en.2: The first store closed at six. The student center one is open until nine.
why_wrong_en.3: The opposite. One store is still open.

questions.analogy_id: **The one** itu kayak nunjuk ke kembarannya: toko lain yang fungsinya sama.
questions.analogy_en: **The one** is pointing to a twin: another store doing the same job.
questions.tip_id: Ada dua jam beda di satu kalimat? Pasangin tiap jam sama tempatnya.
questions.tip_en: Two times in one sentence? Pair each time with its place.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: I'm thinking of taking the eight a.m. statistics section.

script.speaker: M1
script.text: Are you sure? You've been late to every morning class this semester.

questions.prompt: What does the man imply?
options: Statistics is too difficult for her.
He has already taken the course.
The eight a.m. section is full.
She may have trouble attending an early class.
questions.key_sentence: Are you sure? You've been late to every morning class this semester.
questions.key_translation_id: Yakin? Semester ini kamu terlambat di setiap kelas pagi.
questions.why_correct_id: **Are you sure?** nunjukin keraguan. Alasannya, si wanita selalu telat di tiap kelas pagi. Jadi si pria nyiratin kalau kelas jam delapan pagi bisa nyusahin dia.
questions.why_correct_en: **Are you sure?** shows doubt. She's been late to every morning class. So he hints that an 8 a.m. class may be a problem for her.

why_wrong_id.0: Susah nggaknya statistika nggak dibahas. Yang dibahas jamnya.
why_wrong_id.1: Nggak ada info si pria pernah ambil kelas itu.
why_wrong_id.2: Kuota kelas nggak disebut.

why_wrong_en.0: The subject's difficulty isn't discussed. The time is.
why_wrong_en.1: Nothing says he took the course.
why_wrong_en.2: Class capacity isn't mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: **Are you sure?** plus bukti masa lalu itu kayak teman yang ngingetin rekor jelekmu sebelum kamu bikin janji baru.
questions.analogy_en: **Are you sure?** plus past evidence is a friend reminding you of your track record before a new promise.
questions.tip_id: Pertanyaan balik kayak **Are you sure?** atau **Really?** plus fakta artinya ragu. Cari opsi soal masalah yang mungkin muncul.
questions.tip_en: A question back like **Are you sure?** or **Really?** plus a fact means doubt. Look for the likely problem.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Did you finish the lab report, or are you still working on the graphs?

script.speaker: W2
script.text: The graphs are done. It's the conclusion I'm stuck on.

questions.prompt: What does the woman mean?
options: She has not started the report.
She needs help making the graphs.
She is having trouble writing the conclusion.
She has finished the whole report.
questions.key_sentence: It's the conclusion I'm stuck on.
questions.why_correct_id: **The graphs are done** artinya grafiknya udah kelar. **It's the conclusion I'm stuck on** artinya dia buntu di bagian kesimpulan. Jadi dia kesulitan nulis kesimpulannya.
questions.why_correct_en: **The graphs are done** means the graphs are finished. **It's the conclusion I'm stuck on** means she's stuck there. So the conclusion is the trouble.

why_wrong_id.0: Grafiknya udah kelar, berarti laporannya udah dimulai.
why_wrong_id.1: Grafiknya udah kelar. Dia nggak butuh bantuan di situ.
why_wrong_id.3: Kesimpulannya belum kelar, jadi laporannya belum beres.

why_wrong_en.0: The graphs are done, so she has started.
why_wrong_en.1: The graphs are finished. No help needed there.
why_wrong_en.3: The conclusion isn't done, so neither is the report.

questions.analogy_id: **Stuck on** itu kayak mobil yang nyangkut di lumpur. Udah jalan jauh, tapi berhenti di satu titik.
questions.analogy_en: **Stuck on** is a car caught in mud. It got far, but it's stopped at one point.
questions.tip_id: Pola **It's X that…** nekenin X. Jawabannya hampir selalu soal X.
questions.tip_en: **It's X that…** stresses X. The answer is almost always about X.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Did you see the email about the new recycling program in the dorms?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: I did. Starting next Monday, each floor gets three bins: blue for paper, green for glass, and yellow for plastic and cans.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: What about food waste? That's what fills up our trash the most.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: That's the second phase. They'll add compost bins in the kitchens in March, after they see how the first phase goes.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Makes sense. Do we have to wash the containers before we recycle them?

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Just rinse them. The email said dirty containers can ruin a whole bag of recycling.

script.speaker: W1
script.text: Good to know. I'll put a sign on our kitchen door so everyone remembers the colors.

script.speaker: M2
script.text: Great idea. Maybe add a note about rinsing, too.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers mainly discussing?
options: A new recycling system in their dormitory
A cleaning schedule for the kitchen
A broken trash bin on their floor
questions.key_sentence: Did you see the email about the new recycling program in the dorms?
questions.key_translation_id: Kamu sudah lihat email tentang program daur ulang baru di asrama?
questions.why_correct_id: Kalimat pembukanya udah nyebut topik: program daur ulang baru di asrama. Seluruh obrolan bahas aturannya: warna tempat sampah, tahap kedua buat sisa makanan, dan cara ngebilas wadah.
questions.why_correct_en: The opening line names the topic: the new recycling program in the dorms. The rest covers the rules: bin colours, the food-waste phase, rinsing containers.

why_wrong_id.1: Dapur disebut sebagai tempat buat tempat kompos dan papan tanda, bukan jadwal bersih-bersih.
why_wrong_id.2: Nggak ada tempat sampah yang rusak.
why_wrong_id.3: Email itu soal program daur ulang. Nggak disebut kalau emailnya dari dosen.

why_wrong_en.1: The kitchen is where compost bins and a sign go, not a cleaning schedule.
why_wrong_en.2: No bin is broken.
why_wrong_en.3: The email is about the program. Nothing says it's from a professor.

questions.analogy_id: Kalimat pembuka itu kayak judul berita: program daur ulang baru di asrama. Sisanya isi beritanya.
questions.analogy_en: The opening line is the headline: new recycling program in the dorms. The rest is the story.
questions.tip_id: Buat soal topik, pilih jawaban yang nyakup seluruh obrolan, bukan satu detail kayak email atau dapur.
questions.tip_en: For topic questions, pick what covers the whole talk, not one detail like the email or kitchen.

questions.prompt: Which bin should be used for glass?
questions.key_sentence: blue for paper, green for glass, and yellow for plastic and cans.
questions.key_translation_id: biru untuk kertas, hijau untuk kaca, dan kuning untuk plastik dan kaleng.
questions.why_correct_id: Si pria nyebut tiga tempat sampah lengkap sama warnanya. Urutannya: biru buat kertas, HIJAU buat kaca, kuning buat plastik dan kaleng. Jadi kaca masuk tempat sampah hijau.
questions.why_correct_en: He lists three bins with colours: blue for paper, GREEN for glass, yellow for plastic and cans. So glass goes in the green bin.

why_wrong_id.0: Biru buat kertas.
why_wrong_id.2: Kuning buat plastik dan kaleng.
why_wrong_id.3: Tempat kompos buat sisa makanan, dan baru datang bulan Maret.

why_wrong_en.0: Blue is for paper.
why_wrong_en.2: Yellow is for plastic and cans.
why_wrong_en.3: Compost bins are for food waste and only arrive in March.

questions.analogy_id: Daftar warna kayak gini itu kayak kode loker. Catat pasangan warna sama isinya, bukan cuma warnanya.
questions.analogy_en: A colour list is a locker code. Write each colour with its contents, not just the colours.
questions.tip_id: Denger daftar kayak **X for A, Y for B**? Tulis pasangannya singkat: biru-kertas, hijau-kaca.
questions.tip_en: Hear a list like **X for A, Y for B**? Jot the pairs: blue-paper, green-glass.

questions.prompt: When will compost bins be added?
options: At the end of the year
questions.key_sentence: They'll add compost bins in the kitchens in March, after they see how the first phase goes.
questions.key_translation_id: Mereka akan menambah tempat kompos di dapur pada bulan Maret, setelah melihat hasil tahap pertama.
questions.why_correct_id: Tempat kompos disebut sebagai **the second phase**, tahap kedua. Waktunya disebut jelas: **in March**, habis lihat hasil tahap pertama.
questions.why_correct_en: Compost bins are **the second phase**. The timing is clear: **in March**, after seeing how phase one goes.

why_wrong_id.0: **Next Monday** itu waktu mulainya tahap pertama, tiga tempat sampah, bukan tempat kompos.
why_wrong_id.1: Nggak disebut kalau tempat kompos nunggu permintaan mahasiswa.
why_wrong_id.3: Akhir tahun nggak disebut.

why_wrong_en.0: **Next Monday** is when phase one, the three bins, starts. Not the compost bins.
why_wrong_en.1: Nothing says compost bins wait for student requests.
why_wrong_en.3: The end of the year isn't mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: Dua tahap dengan dua waktu itu kayak dua halte bus. Senin depan buat tahap pertama, Maret buat tahap kedua.
questions.analogy_en: Two phases, two dates, like two bus stops. Next Monday for phase one, March for phase two.
questions.tip_id: Obrolan dengan beberapa waktu kayak **next Monday** dan **March**? Cocokin tiap waktu sama kegiatannya.
questions.tip_en: Several times in a talk, like **next Monday** and **March**? Match each to its activity.

script.speaker: LEC
script.text: Today we're going to talk about a small object that changed communication: the postage stamp. Before 1840, sending a letter in Britain was complicated and expensive. The cost depended on the distance and on the number of sheets of paper, and it was usually the person who received the letter, not the sender, who paid. Many people simply refused to accept letters, so the post office often delivered mail and received nothing. In 1837, a teacher named Rowland Hill proposed a simple solution. First, the price should be the same for any distance within the country. Second, the sender should pay in advance. And third, payment would be shown with a small printed label that could be stuck onto the envelope. Parliament accepted the plan, and in May 1840 the world's first adhesive stamp, called the Penny Black, went on sale. The results were dramatic. The number of letters sent in Britain more than doubled within a year. Other countries soon followed. Brazil introduced stamps in 1843, and the United States issued its first national stamps in 1847.

questions.prompt: What is the lecture mainly about?
options: Why letters were expensive to write
The life of a famous British teacher
How the first postage stamp changed the mail system
questions.key_sentence: Today we're going to talk about a small object that changed communication: the postage stamp.
questions.key_translation_id: Hari ini kita akan membahas benda kecil yang mengubah komunikasi: perangko.
questions.why_correct_id: Kalimat pembukanya nyebut topik: perangko, benda kecil yang ngubah cara orang berkomunikasi. Isi kuliahnya: masalah pos sebelum 1840, usulan Rowland Hill, perangko pertama, dan dampaknya.
questions.why_correct_en: The opening names the topic: the postage stamp, a small object that changed communication. Then: the problem before 1840, Hill's proposal, the first stamp, and its impact.

why_wrong_id.0: Yang mahal itu NGIRIM surat, bukan nulisnya. Itu pun cuma latar belakang.
why_wrong_id.1: Rowland Hill disebut karena usulannya, bukan kisah hidupnya.
why_wrong_id.3: Cara nyetak perangko zaman sekarang nggak dibahas.

why_wrong_en.0: Sending, not writing, was expensive, and that's just background.
why_wrong_en.1: Rowland Hill appears for his proposal, not his life story.
why_wrong_en.3: Modern printing isn't covered.

questions.analogy_id: Topik kuliah itu kayak nama mata pelajaran di jadwal. Disebut di awal, terus seluruh isi kelas ngejelasinnya.
questions.analogy_en: A lecture's topic is the subject name on a timetable. Stated first, then the whole class explains it.
questions.tip_id: Opsi topik yang cuma bahas latar belakang, kayak kenapa mahal, biasanya kesempitan.
questions.tip_en: A topic option about background alone, like why it was expensive, is usually too narrow.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was NOT part of Rowland Hill's proposal?
options: A single price for any distance
Payment by the sender in advance
A printed label stuck on the envelope
A higher price for letters with more pages
questions.key_sentence: First, the price should be the same for any distance within the country.
questions.key_translation_id: Pertama, harganya harus sama untuk jarak berapa pun di dalam negeri.
questions.why_correct_id: Dosennya nyebut tiga bagian usulan pakai penanda urutan. **First**: harga sama buat jarak berapa pun. **Second**: pengirim bayar duluan. **And third**: label cetak yang ditempel. Harga berdasarkan jumlah halaman justru sistem LAMA sebelum 1840, bukan usulan Hill.
questions.why_correct_en: The lecturer lists three parts. **First**: one price for any distance. **Second**: the sender pays in advance. **And third**: a printed label. Pricing by pages was the OLD system before 1840, not Hill's idea.

why_wrong_id.0: Disebut sebagai bagian pertama, **First**.
why_wrong_id.1: Disebut sebagai bagian kedua, **Second**.
why_wrong_id.2: Disebut sebagai bagian ketiga, **And third**.

why_wrong_en.0: It's the first part, **First**.
why_wrong_en.1: It's the second part, **Second**.
why_wrong_en.2: It's the third part, **And third**.

questions.analogy_id: Penanda **First**, **Second**, **And third** itu kayak nomor rak. Tiga rak udah keisi, dan opsi keempat nggak punya rak di usulan Hill.
questions.analogy_en: **First**, **Second**, **And third** are shelf numbers. Three shelves are filled, and the fourth option has no shelf in Hill's plan.
questions.tip_id: Pas dosen bilang **First… Second… Third…**, nomorin catatanmu. Soal NOT sering nguji daftar kayak gini.
questions.tip_en: When a lecturer says **First… Second… Third…**, number your notes. NOT questions love these lists.

questions.prompt: What happened to the number of letters sent in Britain after stamps were introduced?
options: It more than doubled within a year.
questions.key_sentence: The number of letters sent in Britain more than doubled within a year.
questions.key_translation_id: Jumlah surat yang dikirim di Inggris naik lebih dari dua kali lipat dalam setahun.
questions.why_correct_id: Habis **The results were dramatic**, dosennya nyebut hasilnya. Jumlah surat **more than doubled within a year**, naik lebih dari dua kali lipat dalam setahun.
questions.why_correct_en: After **The results were dramatic**, the lecturer gives the result. Letters **more than doubled within a year**.

why_wrong_id.0: Kebalikannya. Jumlah suratnya naik, bukan turun.
why_wrong_id.2: 1843 itu tahun Brasil ngenalin perangko, bukan tahun perubahan di Inggris.
why_wrong_id.3: Kuliahnya cuma bilang naik lebih dari dua kali lipat dalam SETAHUN, bukan tiap tahun sampai 1847.

why_wrong_en.0: The opposite. Letters went up, not down.
why_wrong_en.2: 1843 is when Brazil introduced stamps, not a change in Britain.
why_wrong_en.3: It more than doubled within ONE year, not every year until 1847.

questions.analogy_id: **The results were dramatic** itu kayak bunyi drum sebelum pengumuman juara. Angka penting bakal segera disebut.
questions.analogy_en: **The results were dramatic** is a drumroll before the winner. An important number is coming.
questions.tip_id: Kata **dramatic**, **surprising**, **remarkable** sering muncul pas sebelum angka yang ditanya.
questions.tip_en: **Dramatic**, **surprising**, **remarkable** often come right before the number being tested.

items.prompt: The scientists made an important ______ about the origin of the disease.
items.why_correct_id: Habis **an important**, article plus adjective (kata sifat), butuh noun (kata benda). Akhiran -y di **discovery** nandain kata benda. Jawabannya **discovery**.
items.why_correct_en: After **an important**, article plus adjective, you need a noun. **discovery** is the noun form. That's the answer.

why_wrong_id.1: **discover** itu kata kerja. Nggak bisa nongol setelah **an important**.
why_wrong_id.2: **discovered** itu V2/V3, bukan kata benda.
why_wrong_id.3: **discovering** (V-ing) nggak pas di sini. **make a discovery** itu pasangan kata yang udah paten.

why_wrong_en.1: **discover** is a verb. It can't follow **an important**.
why_wrong_en.2: **discovered** is V2/V3, not a noun.
why_wrong_en.3: **discovering** doesn't fit. **make a discovery** is a fixed pairing.

items.analogy_id: Article plus kata sifat itu kayak kursi yang udah disiapin. Yang duduk harus kata benda.
items.analogy_en: Article plus adjective is a seat already set out. Only a noun sits there.

items.prompt: The museum guide spoke ______ about the history of the paintings.
items.why_correct_id: Kata yang hilang nerangin cara si pemandu ngomong, alias nerangin kata kerja **spoke**. Yang nerangin kata kerja itu [[adverb]], biasanya akhirannya -ly: **enthusiastically**.
items.why_correct_en: The missing word tells how the guide spoke, so it modifies **spoke**. Verbs take adverbs, usually ending in -ly: **enthusiastically**.

why_wrong_id.0: **enthusiasm** itu kata benda, semangat. Nggak bisa langsung nerangin kata kerja.
why_wrong_id.1: **enthusiastic** itu adjective (kata sifat). Kata sifat nerangin kata benda, bukan kata kerja.
why_wrong_id.2: **enthusiast** itu kata benda buat orang, penggemar.

why_wrong_en.0: **enthusiasm** is a noun. It can't directly modify a verb.
why_wrong_en.1: **enthusiastic** is an adjective. Adjectives describe nouns, not verbs.
why_wrong_en.2: **enthusiast** is a noun for a person, a fan.

items.analogy_id: Adverb itu gaya nyetir. Dia nerangin GIMANA mesinnya, **spoke**, jalan.
items.analogy_en: An adverb is driving style. It tells HOW the engine, **spoke**, runs.
items.tip_id: Kata kerja aksi plus ___ yang jawab gimana? Pilih bentuk -ly.
items.tip_en: Action verb plus ___ answering how? Choose the -ly form.

items.prompt: The new policy had a ______ effect on student attendance.
items.why_correct_id: Rumpangnya ada di antara **a** dan kata benda **effect**. Posisi sebelum kata benda diisi [[adjective]]. Akhiran -ant nandain kata sifat: **significant**.
items.why_correct_en: The blank sits between **a** and the noun **effect**. Before a noun goes an adjective. The -ant ending marks one: **significant**.

why_wrong_id.0: **signify** itu kata kerja.
why_wrong_id.1: **significance** itu kata benda. Dua kata benda jejer, **a significance effect**, nggak pas di sini.
why_wrong_id.3: **significantly** itu adverb (kata keterangan). Adverb nggak nerangin kata benda.

why_wrong_en.0: **signify** is a verb.
why_wrong_en.1: **significance** is a noun. **a significance effect** doesn't work here.
why_wrong_en.3: **significantly** is an adverb. Adverbs don't describe nouns.

items.analogy_id: Adjective itu cat mobil. Dioles langsung ke bendanya, **effect**.
items.analogy_en: An adjective is paint, applied straight onto the thing, **effect**.
items.tip_id: **a/an + ___ + kata benda** butuh kata sifat. Hafalin akhirannya: -ant/-ent, -ous, -ive, -ful, -al.
items.tip_en: **a/an + ___ + noun** needs an adjective. Learn the endings: -ant/-ent, -ous, -ive, -ful, -al.

items.prompt: Many students find it ______ to study in a quiet library than at home.
items.why_correct_id: Pola **find it + ___ + to …** butuh [[adjective]] setelah **it**, kayak **find it easy** atau **find it difficult**. Ada **than**, jadi butuh bentuk perbandingan. Kata sifat plus perbandingan jadinya **more productive**.
items.why_correct_en: **find it + ___ + to …** needs an adjective after **it**, like **find it easy**. **than** calls for a comparative. So: **more productive**.

why_wrong_id.0: **more productively** itu adverb. Habis **find it** butuh kata sifat.
why_wrong_id.2: **productivity** itu kata benda dan nggak bisa dibandingin pakai **than** di pola ini.
why_wrong_id.3: **most produce** pakai kata kerja dan superlative. Dua-duanya nggak cocok sama **than**.

why_wrong_en.0: **more productively** is an adverb. **find it** needs an adjective.
why_wrong_en.2: **productivity** is a noun and doesn't fit this **than** comparison.
why_wrong_en.3: **most produce** uses a verb and a superlative. Neither fits **than**.

items.analogy_id: **Find it ___** itu kayak ngasih nilai ke sesuatu. Nilainya berupa sifat (**productive**), bukan cara (**productively**).
items.analogy_en: **Find it ___** gives something a rating. The rating is a quality (**productive**), not a manner (**productively**).
items.tip_id: **find/make/consider + it + KATA SIFAT + to V1**. Jangan kejebak bentuk -ly.
items.tip_en: **find/make/consider + it + ADJECTIVE + to V1**. Don't fall for -ly forms.

items.prompt: The {A}manager{/A} gave a {B}clearly{/B} {C}explanation{/C} of the new {D}rules{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: **clearly** nongkrong di antara **a** dan kata benda **explanation**. Posisi sebelum kata benda butuh [[adjective]], bukan adverb. Jadi **clearly** harus jadi **clear**.
items.why_correct_en: **clearly** sits between **a** and the noun **explanation**. Before a noun you need an adjective, not an adverb. So **clearly** should be **clear**.

why_wrong_id.0: **manager** itu kata benda yang pas jadi pelaku.
why_wrong_id.2: **explanation** itu kata benda yang pas setelah kata sifat.
why_wrong_id.3: **the new rules** itu frasa benda yang aman.

why_wrong_en.0: **manager** is a fine noun subject.
why_wrong_en.2: **explanation** is a fine noun after the adjective.
why_wrong_en.3: **the new rules** is a fine noun phrase.

items.analogy_id: Adverb di depan kata benda itu kayak stiker gaya nyetir yang ditempel di cat mobil. Salah tempat.
items.analogy_en: An adverb before a noun is a driving-style sticker slapped on the paint. Wrong place.
items.tip_id: **a/an + ___ + kata benda**: ada -ly di posisi itu? Hampir pasti salah.
items.tip_en: **a/an + ___ + noun**: an -ly word there is almost always wrong.

items.why_correct_id: Habis **The**, dan posisinya sebagai pelaku kalimat, butuh kata benda. **govern** itu kata kerja. Bentuk kata bendanya **government**, akhiran -ment.
items.why_correct_en: After **The**, in the subject slot, you need a noun. **govern** is a verb. The noun is **government**, with -ment.

why_wrong_id.1: **measures**, langkah-langkah, itu kata benda jamak yang aman.
why_wrong_id.2: **to reduce** itu infinitive (to + kata kerja dasar) yang aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **air pollution** itu frasa benda yang aman.

why_wrong_en.1: **measures** is a fine plural noun.
why_wrong_en.2: **to reduce** is a fine infinitive.
why_wrong_en.3: **air pollution** is a fine noun phrase.

items.analogy_id: Kursi sopir cuma buat kata benda. **Govern** masih pakai seragam kata kerja, jadi harus ganti seragam jadi **government**.
items.analogy_en: The driver's seat is noun-only. **Govern** is still in a verb uniform. It has to change into **government**.
items.tip_id: **The + ___ + kata kerja**? Berarti ___ harus kata benda. Cek akhiran -ment, -tion, -ity.
items.tip_en: **The + ___ + verb**? Then ___ must be a noun. Look for -ment, -tion, -ity.

items.prompt: Regular exercise {A}improves{/A} both physical and mental {B}healthy{/B} and {C}reduces{/C} {D}stress{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: **improves both physical and mental ___** butuh objek berupa kata benda. **physical** dan **mental** itu kata sifat yang nerangin dia. Masalahnya, **healthy** itu kata sifat. Kata bendanya **health**.
items.why_correct_en: **improves both physical and mental ___** needs a noun object. **physical** and **mental** describe it. But **healthy** is an adjective. The noun is **health**.

why_wrong_id.0: **improves** itu tunggal, cocok sama **Regular exercise**.
why_wrong_id.2: **reduces** sejajar sama **improves**. Aman.
why_wrong_id.3: **stress** itu kata benda yang pas jadi objek **reduces**.

why_wrong_en.0: **improves** is singular, matching **Regular exercise**.
why_wrong_en.2: **reduces** is parallel with **improves**. Fine.
why_wrong_en.3: **stress** is a fine noun object of **reduces**.

items.analogy_id: Dua kata sifat, **physical** dan **mental**, itu cat. Cat butuh benda buat dioles: **health**, bukan **healthy**.
items.analogy_en: Two adjectives, **physical** and **mental**, are paint. Paint needs a thing to cover: **health**, not **healthy**.
items.tip_id: Kata sifat plus ___ di ujung frasa? Berarti ___ harus kata benda.
items.tip_en: Adjective plus ___ at the end of a phrase? Then ___ must be a noun.

items.prompt: The {A}construct{/A} of the new library {B}took{/B} nearly two years because of {C}frequent{/C} {D}delays{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: **The ___ of the new library** itu pelaku, jadi butuh kata benda. **construct** itu kata kerja. Kata bendanya **construction**, akhiran -tion.
items.why_correct_en: **The ___ of the new library** is the subject, so it needs a noun. **construct** is a verb. The noun is **construction**, with -tion.

why_wrong_id.1: **took** itu V2 dari **take**. Cocok buat kejadian lampau.
why_wrong_id.2: **frequent** itu kata sifat yang nerangin **delays**.
why_wrong_id.3: **delays** itu kata benda jamak yang pas setelah **because of**.

why_wrong_en.1: **took** is the V2 of **take**, fitting a past event.
why_wrong_en.2: **frequent** is an adjective describing **delays**.
why_wrong_en.3: **delays** is a fine plural noun after **because of**.

items.analogy_id: Pola **The ___ of …** itu kayak bingkai foto yang cuma muat benda, bukan aksi.
items.analogy_en: **The ___ of …** is a picture frame that only fits a thing, not an action.
items.tip_id: **The + ___ + of**? Butuh kata benda. Ubah kata kerjanya jadi -tion, -ment, atau -ance.
items.tip_en: **The + ___ + of**? You need a noun. Turn the verb into -tion, -ment, or -ance.

items.prompt: The village is {A}famous{/A} for its {B}traditional{/B} music and {C}colorful{/C} {D}decorate{/D}.
items.why_correct_id: **its traditional music and colorful ___** nyejajarin dua frasa benda. Habis kata sifat **colorful** butuh kata benda. **decorate** itu kata kerja. Kata bendanya **decorations**.
items.why_correct_en: **its traditional music and colorful ___** pairs two noun phrases. After **colorful** you need a noun. **decorate** is a verb. The noun is **decorations**.

why_wrong_id.0: **famous for** itu pola kata sifat plus kata depan yang aman.
why_wrong_id.1: **traditional** itu kata sifat yang nerangin **music**.
why_wrong_id.2: **colorful** itu kata sifat yang pas sebelum kata benda.

why_wrong_en.0: **famous for** is a fine adjective plus preposition.
why_wrong_en.1: **traditional** is an adjective describing **music**.
why_wrong_en.2: **colorful** fits nicely before a noun.

items.analogy_id: Dua gerbong yang digandeng **and** harus sejenis: **music**, benda, dan **decorations**, benda.
items.analogy_en: Two carriages linked by **and** must match: **music**, a thing, and **decorations**, a thing.
items.tip_id: Habis **and**, cek bentuknya sama nggak kayak bagian sebelum **and**.
items.tip_en: After **and**, check the form matches the part before it.

items.prompt: The committee praised her {A}persistent{/A} effort and her {B}creative{/B} approach, which {C}success{/C} {D}solved{/D} the problem.
items.why_correct_id: Di clause **which ___ solved the problem**, **which** itu pelaku dan **solved** itu kata kerja. Kata di antara keduanya yang nerangin cara nyelesaiinnya itu [[adverb]]. **success** itu kata benda. Adverb-nya **successfully**.
items.why_correct_en: In **which ___ solved the problem**, **which** is the subject and **solved** the verb. A word between them telling how is an adverb. **success** is a noun. The adverb is **successfully**.

why_wrong_id.0: **persistent** itu kata sifat yang pas sebelum **effort**.
why_wrong_id.1: **creative** itu kata sifat yang pas sebelum **approach**.
why_wrong_id.3: **solved** (V2) itu kata kerja yang pas buat **which**.

why_wrong_en.0: **persistent** fits before **effort**.
why_wrong_en.1: **creative** fits before **approach**.
why_wrong_en.3: **solved** (V2) is the right verb for **which**.

items.analogy_id: Di antara sopir (**which**) dan mesin (**solved**) cuma ada ruang buat gaya nyetir, yaitu adverb.
items.analogy_en: Between the driver (**which**) and the engine (**solved**) there's only room for driving style: an adverb.
items.tip_id: **Pelaku + ___ + kata kerja**? ___ biasanya adverb (-ly). Kata benda di posisi itu hampir pasti salah.
items.tip_en: **Subject + ___ + verb**? ___ is usually an adverb (-ly). A noun there is almost always wrong.

items.title: Science at the Bottom of the World
items.body:
Antarctica is the coldest, driest, and windiest continent on Earth, and no one lives there permanently. Yet it is home to dozens of research stations operated by countries from around the world. In winter, only about a thousand people remain on the continent, but in the summer months the population rises to several thousand as scientists arrive to take advantage of the long hours of daylight.

The continent is managed under the Antarctic Treaty, which was signed in 1959 by twelve countries and has since been joined by many more. The treaty sets aside Antarctica for peaceful purposes and for scientific research. Military bases and weapons testing are forbidden, and a later agreement banned mining. Countries may not use their research stations to claim new territory.

Why do scientists accept such difficult conditions? One reason is that Antarctica offers records of the past found nowhere else. By drilling deep into the ice sheet, researchers can remove long cylinders of ice called ice cores. Tiny bubbles trapped in the ice contain samples of ancient air, allowing scientists to measure how the atmosphere has changed over hundreds of thousands of years.

Antarctica is also an excellent place to observe the sky. The air is dry and clean, and there is almost no light pollution, so telescopes can see faint objects clearly. In addition, meteorites that fall onto the ice are easy to spot against the white surface, and many important specimens have been collected there.

Finally, the continent plays an important role in monitoring the health of the planet. It was at an Antarctic station that British scientists first reported, in 1985, a dramatic thinning of the ozone layer, a discovery that led to international action to limit harmful chemicals.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 2, the Antarctic Treaty forbids all of the following EXCEPT
questions.evidence_quote: The treaty sets aside Antarctica for peaceful purposes and for scientific research.
questions.why_correct_id: Baca paragraf 2 dan centang yang dilarang: pangkalan militer dilarang, uji senjata dilarang, klaim wilayah baru juga nggak boleh. Penelitian ilmiah justru salah satu tujuan perjanjiannya, **for scientific research**. Jadi penelitian ilmiah itu pengecualiannya.
questions.why_correct_en: Read paragraph 2 and tick what's banned: military bases, weapons testing, new territory claims. Scientific research is one of the treaty's purposes, **for scientific research**. So research is the exception.

why_wrong_id.0: Pangkalan militer disebut dilarang, **Military bases … are forbidden**.
why_wrong_id.1: Uji senjata disebut dilarang.
why_wrong_id.3: Negara nggak boleh make stasiunnya buat ngeklaim wilayah baru.

why_wrong_en.0: Military bases are forbidden.
why_wrong_en.1: Weapons testing is forbidden.
why_wrong_en.3: Stations may not be used to claim new territory.

questions.analogy_id: Soal EXCEPT itu kayak absen kelas. Tiga opsi jawab dilarang, satu opsi diem karena justru dibolehin.
questions.analogy_en: An EXCEPT question is a roll call. Three options answer banned, one stays quiet because it's allowed.
questions.tip_id: Di soal EXCEPT, jawabannya sering justru sesuatu yang DIDUKUNG teks, kebalikan dari kelompoknya.
questions.tip_en: In EXCEPT questions, the answer is often something the text SUPPORTS, the opposite of the group.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the population of Antarctica increase in summer?
options: Tourists arrive to see the ice.
Scientists come to use the long hours of daylight.
Military bases open for the season.
Miners are allowed to work there.
questions.evidence_quote: in the summer months the population rises to several thousand as scientists arrive to take advantage of the long hours of daylight.
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kunci **summer** ada di akhir paragraf 1. Populasinya naik karena ilmuwan datang buat manfaatin siang yang panjang.
questions.why_correct_en: **summer** is at the end of paragraph 1. The population rises as scientists come to use the long daylight.

why_wrong_id.0: Wisatawan nggak disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Pangkalan militer dilarang sama perjanjiannya.
why_wrong_id.3: Pertambangan dilarang sama perjanjian berikutnya.

why_wrong_en.0: Tourists aren't mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: Military bases are banned by the treaty.
why_wrong_en.3: Mining is banned by a later agreement.

questions.analogy_id: Kata **as** di sini artinya karena atau ketika. Dia nyambungin naiknya populasi sama penyebabnya.
questions.analogy_en: **As** here means because or when. It links the population rise to its cause.
questions.tip_id: Soal **why** nggak selalu pakai **because**. Kata **as**, **since**, **so** juga bisa ngasih alasan.
questions.tip_en: **Why** answers don't always use **because**. **as**, **since**, and **so** give reasons too.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a reason Antarctica is a good place to observe the sky?
options: The nights are always free of clouds.
questions.evidence_quote: The air is dry and clean, and there is almost no light pollution, so telescopes can see faint objects clearly.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 4 nyebut alasannya: udara kering, udara bersih, dan hampir nggak ada polusi cahaya. Centang ketiganya. Malam yang selalu tanpa awan sama sekali nggak disebut. Itulah jawabannya.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 4 gives the reasons: dry air, clean air, almost no light pollution. Tick all three. Always cloudless nights is never mentioned. That's the answer.

why_wrong_id.0: Udara kering disebut, **The air is dry**.
why_wrong_id.1: Polusi cahaya yang hampir nggak ada disebut.
why_wrong_id.2: Udara bersih disebut, **and clean**.

why_wrong_en.0: Dry air is mentioned.
why_wrong_en.1: Almost no light pollution is mentioned.
why_wrong_en.2: Clean air is mentioned, **and clean**.

questions.analogy_id: Opsi yang kedengeran masuk akal tapi nggak tertulis itu kayak tamu nggak diundang. Kelihatan cocok, tapi namanya nggak ada di daftar.
questions.analogy_en: A plausible option that isn't written is an uninvited guest. It fits in, but its name isn't on the list.
questions.tip_id: Opsi dengan kata mutlak kayak **always** atau **never** yang nggak ada di teks sering jadi jawaban soal NOT MENTIONED.
questions.tip_en: Absolute words like **always** or **never** that aren't in the text often mark the NOT MENTIONED answer.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the bubbles in ice cores contain?
questions.evidence_quote: Tiny bubbles trapped in the ice contain samples of ancient air
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kunci **bubbles** ada di paragraf 3. Gelembung kecil di dalam es isinya sampel udara purba.
questions.why_correct_en: **bubbles** is in paragraph 3. The tiny bubbles hold samples of ancient air.

why_wrong_id.1: Meteorit jatuh di permukaan es, paragraf 4, bukan di dalam gelembung.
why_wrong_id.2: Bahan kimia berbahaya disebut soal lapisan ozon, paragraf 5.
why_wrong_id.3: Air laut beku nggak disebut.

why_wrong_en.1: Meteorites land on the ice surface, paragraph 4, not inside bubbles.
why_wrong_en.2: Harmful chemicals relate to the ozone layer, paragraph 5.
why_wrong_en.3: Frozen seawater isn't mentioned.

questions.analogy_id: Gelembung di es itu kayak kapsul waktu. Nyimpen udara dari ratusan ribu tahun lalu.
questions.analogy_en: Bubbles in ice are time capsules holding air from hundreds of thousands of years ago.
questions.tip_id: Pengecoh soal detail sering dicomot dari paragraf lain, kayak meteorit atau bahan kimia. Cek paragrafnya.
questions.tip_en: Detail distractors often come from other paragraphs, like meteorites or chemicals. Check the paragraph.

questions.prompt: Why does the author mention the thinning of the ozone layer in paragraph 5?
options: To show that Antarctica is getting colder
To give an example of Antarctica's role in monitoring the planet
To argue that mining should be allowed
questions.evidence_quote: Finally, the continent plays an important role in monitoring the health of the planet.
questions.why_correct_id: Kalimat pertama paragraf 5 udah nyatain gagasannya: Antarktika berperan mantau kesehatan planet. Penemuan penipisan ozon tahun 1985 itu contoh nyata peran tersebut.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 5 opens with its idea: Antarctica helps monitor the planet's health. The 1985 ozone discovery is a concrete example.

why_wrong_id.0: Suhu Antarktika yang makin dingin nggak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.2: Teleskop dibahas di paragraf 4.
why_wrong_id.3: Pertambangan dilarang. Penulis nggak ndukung itu.

why_wrong_en.0: Antarctica getting colder isn't discussed.
why_wrong_en.2: Telescopes are in paragraph 4.
why_wrong_en.3: Mining is banned. The author doesn't argue for it.

questions.analogy_id: Contoh dalam paragraf itu kayak foto bukti di laporan. Dia nunjukin klaim di kalimat pertama itu bener.
questions.analogy_en: An example is a photo in a report. Proof that the first sentence's claim holds.
questions.tip_id: Soal **Why does the author mention X?** Baca kalimat pertama paragraf X. Biasanya X itu contohnya.
questions.tip_en: **Why does the author mention X?** Read the first sentence of X's paragraph. X is usually its example.

items.title: A Drink That Traveled the World
items.body:
Tea is the most widely consumed drink in the world after water, but for most of history it was known only in a small part of Asia. According to Chinese tradition, people in southwestern China were drinking tea thousands of years ago, at first mainly as a medicine.

Over the centuries, tea spread along trade routes. Buddhist monks carried tea seeds from China to Japan, where drinking tea developed into a carefully practiced ceremony. Traders also brought tea across Central Asia and into Russia, where it was often transported by camel caravans.

Tea did not reach Europe as a trade good until the early seventeenth century, when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia. At first it was an expensive luxury. In Britain, tea became fashionable after the Portuguese princess Catherine of Braganza, who was already **fond** of the drink, married King Charles II in 1662. Within a century, tea had become a daily habit for people of all classes.

The British demand for tea was so great that the country wanted to stop depending on China for its supply. In the 1830s, British companies began growing tea in the Assam region of India, where a local variety of the plant was found. Later, plantations were established in what is now Sri Lanka and in East Africa, which are still major producers today.

Even the way tea is prepared has changed. According to a popular story, the tea bag was invented by accident in the early 1900s, when a New York merchant sent samples of tea in small silk bags and customers dropped the bags directly into hot water.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why tea is healthier than coffee
The history of the British royal family
How tea spread from China to the rest of the world
How tea bags are made today
questions.evidence_quote: Over the centuries, tea spread along trade routes.
questions.why_correct_id: Paragraf 1 bilang teh awalnya cuma dikenal di sebagian kecil Asia. Paragraf berikutnya ngikutin penyebarannya: Jepang dan Rusia, Eropa dan Inggris, perkebunan di India dan Afrika, sampai cara nyajinya. Jadi topiknya penyebaran teh ke seluruh dunia.
questions.why_correct_en: Paragraph 1 says tea was once known only in a small part of Asia. Then we follow its spread: Japan and Russia, Europe and Britain, India and Africa, and how it's served. So it's how tea spread worldwide.

why_wrong_id.0: Kopi nggak dibahas.
why_wrong_id.1: Raja Charles II dan Catherine cuma satu contoh di paragraf 3.
why_wrong_id.3: Kantong teh cuma dibahas di paragraf terakhir, dan cara bikinnya sekarang nggak dijelasin.

why_wrong_en.0: Coffee isn't discussed.
why_wrong_en.1: Charles II and Catherine are one example in paragraph 3.
why_wrong_en.3: Tea bags only appear at the end, and modern manufacturing isn't explained.

questions.analogy_id: Teks sejarah kayak gini itu kayak peta perjalanan. Tiap paragraf satu kota yang disinggahi teh.
questions.analogy_en: A history passage like this is a travel map. Each paragraph is a city tea passed through.
questions.tip_id: Paragrafnya ngikutin urutan waktu atau tempat? Ide pokoknya biasanya soal gimana X berkembang atau menyebar.
questions.tip_en: Paragraphs following time or place? The main idea is usually how X grew or spread.

questions.prompt: Which of the following places is NOT mentioned as a place where tea was grown?
questions.evidence_quote: Later, plantations were established in what is now Sri Lanka and in East Africa, which are still major producers today.
questions.why_correct_id: Cari tempat nanam teh di paragraf 4: India (Assam), Sri Lanka, dan Afrika Timur. Rusia disebut di paragraf 2 sebagai tujuan dagang teh lewat karavan unta, bukan tempat nanamnya.
questions.why_correct_en: Find where tea was grown in paragraph 4: India (Assam), Sri Lanka, East Africa. Russia shows up in paragraph 2 as a trade destination, not a growing place.

why_wrong_id.0: India (wilayah Assam) disebut sebagai tempat perusahaan Inggris mulai nanam teh.
why_wrong_id.1: Sri Lanka disebut sebagai tempat perkebunan.
why_wrong_id.2: Afrika Timur disebut sebagai tempat perkebunan.

why_wrong_en.0: India (Assam) is where British companies started growing tea.
why_wrong_en.1: Sri Lanka is named as a plantation spot.
why_wrong_en.2: East Africa is named as a plantation spot.

questions.analogy_id: Rusia di teks ini kayak stasiun tujuan kereta barang. Tehnya dikirim ke sana, bukan ditanam di sana.
questions.analogy_en: Russia here is a freight train's destination. Tea was shipped there, not grown there.
questions.tip_id: Bedain peran tempatnya: asal, tujuan, atau lokasi produksi. Soal NOT sering manfaatin bedanya.
questions.tip_en: Separate a place's role: origin, destination, or production. NOT questions love this.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did tea become fashionable in Britain?
options: A princess who already liked tea married the king.
Doctors recommended it as a medicine.
It was grown in Britain for the first time.
questions.evidence_quote: In Britain, tea became fashionable after the Portuguese princess Catherine of Braganza, who was already fond of the drink, married King Charles II in 1662.
questions.why_correct_id: Kata kunci **fashionable** ada di paragraf 3. Teh jadi tren setelah putri Portugis Catherine, yang udah suka teh, nikah sama Raja Charles II.
questions.why_correct_en: **fashionable** is in paragraph 3. Tea caught on after Catherine, a Portuguese princess already fond of it, married Charles II.

why_wrong_id.1: Pedagang Belanda bawa teh ke Eropa, tapi teks nggak nyebut mereka nurunin harga. Teh malah barang mewah.
why_wrong_id.2: Teh sebagai obat disebut buat Tiongkok kuno di paragraf 1, bukan Inggris.
why_wrong_id.3: Teh nggak ditanam di Inggris. Inggris nanamnya di India.

why_wrong_en.1: Dutch merchants brought tea to Europe, but no price drop is mentioned. It was a luxury.
why_wrong_en.2: Tea as medicine relates to ancient China, paragraph 1, not Britain.
why_wrong_en.3: Tea wasn't grown in Britain. The British grew it in India.

questions.analogy_id: Kayak seleb yang make satu merek tas, terus semua orang ikutan beli.
questions.analogy_en: Like a celebrity carrying one brand of bag, and then everyone buys it too.
questions.tip_id: Kata **after** bisa nunjukin sebab di soal detail sejarah.
questions.tip_en: **After** can signal a cause in history detail questions.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements about tea in Europe are true EXCEPT
options: Europeans drank it before the year 1500.
Dutch merchants were the first to ship it there.
It was at first an expensive luxury.
In Britain it became a habit for all classes.
questions.evidence_quote: Tea did not reach Europe as a trade good until the early seventeenth century, when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia.
questions.why_correct_id: Centang pernyataan yang bener: pedagang Belanda yang ngirim teh, bener. Awalnya barang mewah, bener. Di Inggris jadi kebiasaan semua kalangan, bener. Teks bilang teh baru masuk Eropa sebagai barang dagangan di awal abad ke-17, tahun 1600-an. Jadi sebelum tahun 1500 itu salah.
questions.why_correct_en: Tick the true ones: Dutch merchants shipped it, it was first a luxury, it became a habit for all classes in Britain. Tea first reached Europe as a trade good in the early 1600s. So before 1500 is false.

why_wrong_id.1: Teks: **when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia**.
why_wrong_id.2: Teks: **At first it was an expensive luxury**.
why_wrong_id.3: Teks: **tea had become a daily habit for people of all classes**.

why_wrong_en.1: Text: **when Dutch merchants began shipping it from Asia**.
why_wrong_en.2: Text: **At first it was an expensive luxury**.
why_wrong_en.3: Text: **tea had become a daily habit for people of all classes**.

questions.analogy_id: Abad ke-17 itu tahun 1600-an. Ngubah abad jadi tahun itu kayak ngubah jam tujuh malam jadi 19.00. Artinya sama, angkanya beda.
questions.analogy_en: The seventeenth century is the 1600s. Like turning seven p.m. into 19:00. Same meaning, different numbers.
questions.tip_id: Ubah abad ke-N jadi tahun (N-1)00-an biar opsi yang pakai tahun gampang dicek.
questions.tip_en: Turn the Nth century into the (N-1)00s so year-based options are easy to check.

questions.prompt: The word **fond** in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.evidence_quote: who was already fond of the drink
questions.why_correct_id: Kalimatnya ngejelasin kenapa teh jadi tren habis Catherine nikah: dia udah **fond of the drink**. Orang yang bikin minuman jadi populer pasti suka sama minuman itu. Jadi **fond** artinya **keen**, gemar.
questions.why_correct_en: The sentence explains why tea caught on after Catherine married: she was already **fond of the drink**. Someone who makes a drink popular must like it. So **fond** means **keen**.

why_wrong_id.0: Takut sama teh nggak masuk akal kalau dia yang bikin teh jadi tren.
why_wrong_id.2: Bosen sama teh juga bentrok sama alasan teh jadi populer.
why_wrong_id.3: Dia jelas tahu soal teh, soalnya udah suka dari awal, **already**.

why_wrong_en.0: Being afraid of tea doesn't fit someone who made it fashionable.
why_wrong_en.2: Being tired of it clashes with why it caught on.
why_wrong_en.3: She clearly knew tea, since she **already** liked it.

questions.analogy_id: Kalau seorang putri bikin minuman jadi tren, dia pasti penggemarnya. Bukan orang yang takut atau bosen.
questions.analogy_en: If a princess makes a drink fashionable, she's a fan, not someone scared or bored of it.
questions.tip_id: Cek akibat di kalimatnya, **tea became fashionable**, buat nentuin katanya positif atau negatif.
questions.tip_en: Check the result, **tea became fashionable**, to tell if the word is positive or negative.
